gloss: joruri; narrative chanting for puppet theater

definitions.explanation: A form of dramatic narrative chanting accompanied by shamisen music, traditionally performed as the vocal component of bunraku puppet theater. One of the major traditional performing arts of Japan.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Joruri is one of the traditional performing arts of Japan, closely associated with bunraku puppet theater. The narrator (called ⟦{太夫|たゆう}→太夫：25012_tayuu⟧) chants the story while a shamisen player provides accompaniment. The art form flourished during the Edo period.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{義太夫|ぎだゆう}→義太夫：28510_gidayuu⟧{浄瑠璃|じょうるり} (gidayu-style joruri, the most prominent school)
- {浄瑠璃|じょうるり}⟦{太夫|たゆう}→太夫：25012_tayuu⟧ (joruri narrator)
- {浄瑠璃|じょうるり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{語|かた}る→語る：01930_kataru⟧ (to narrate joruri)

RELATED WORDS:
Closely linked to ⟦{文楽|ぶんらく}→文楽：13156_bunraku⟧ (bunraku puppet theater), where joruri provides the vocal narration.
